facts.topic: attribute replay eligibility and frame boundary
facts.contract: The own-player update listener requires a nonzero packet tick, a ReplayStateComponent with history, and tick >= ActorHistory.mOldestFrame. ActorHistory.mOldestFrame is the PDB-named uint64 member at offset48. ReplayState reads the stamp frame and its following frame; a required retained correction is attached to stamp+1. An ineligible old/zero stamp reaches the ordinary live attribute update path.
anchors: ClientNetworkHandler UpdateAttributes handler RVA0x1311D80; rewind-listener call RVA0x1311ED1
eligibility helper RVA0x4358CD0; zero check RVA0x4358CD0; oldest comparison RVA0x4358DBD
ReplayStateComponent::_applyCorrection RVA0x2890390; stamp+1 RVA0x28903F1; addCorrectionToFrame call RVA0x28905CF

facts.contract: MovementAttributesComponentExt maps nine named attributes to optional floats. Health and hunger use NoRewindNoPrediction; movement, underwater/lava movement, jump strength, friction, bounciness and air drag use RewindIfDifferentPreservePrediction.
anchors: MovementAttributesComponent size72; optional fields every8 bytes
PDB named SharedAttributes globals in attribute_replay_reference.json

facts.contract: For a rewind-enabled entry, getAdvanceFrameResult compares packet current with the saved optional component value using ordered exact float equality and requires the saved optional to be present. Equal present values set MovementAttributeInfo.mSkipUpdate. advanceLiveFrame skips those entries; other entries update the live attribute map with the full AttributeData. Equality is not a comparison of modifiers or default values.
anchors: ordered float equality and optional-presence test RVA0x4375510..RVA0x4375525

facts.topic: pending attribute correction bypasses equality shortcut
facts.contract: AttributeReplay reports correction-type bitset2. ReplayState checks the pending correction types before getAdvanceFrameResult; if that type is pending, it bypasses the equality comparison and still advances the live correction. This matters for several packets drained before the requested replay has completed.

facts.topic: historical replay uses complete attribute records
facts.contract: advanceFrame writes every present value in the correction MovementAttributes snapshot to the historical component, then updates the historical AttributesComponent with full packet AttributeData, including defaults, bounds and modifiers. The historical path does not filter out entries whose live mSkipUpdate was true.
anchors: MovementAttributesComponentExt::create RVA0x28791D0 copies packet current and presence

facts.topic: latest-stamp comparison reads evaluated movement values
facts.contract: If stamp+1 has no captured frame but the stamp exists, _applyCorrection selects the actor entity context. SnapshotAccessor resolves a captured MovementSnapshotComponent when present, otherwise its live MovementAttributesComponent. The captured form contains an unchanged72-byte MovementAttributes copy at offset0x2D0. The compared values are evaluated component values, not the raw packet current or a newly recomputed value using later controls.
anchors: captured component movement offset/presence check RVA0x3298420..RVA0x3298431
live MovementAttributes lookup hash0xA795A68C at RVA0x329845E

implementation.scope: The four already-consumed physics attributes: movement, underwater movement, lava movement and air drag.
changes: Queue full own-player UpdateAttributes entries and stamps in arrival order; stage the four physics attributes until the local simulation consumes them. Health/UI and unrelated attribute handling remain in their existing immediate route.

Capture each frame’s evaluated speed model and optional-presence state, retain accepted attribute boundaries, and recompute corrected history with each frame’s saved sprint and freeze input. Later retained server events are reapplied rather than overwritten.
When a historical next-frame value matches, preserve that live attribute’s current prediction and modifiers. A required mixed correction still retains the complete historical packet entries.
Compare current-tick acknowledgments against the last evaluated retained record, including freeze-derived speed. Changed current-tick values take effect on the next recorded input.
Keep pending live attribute events through a failed input transmission and consume them only when a new frame is recorded; clear local pending events with the world reset.
Do not mutate the live speed model while evaluating historical sprint/freeze transitions.

implementation.verification: Final Linux application build, attribute_replay_selftest (150 checks), handler_dispatch_selftest, movement_protocol_selftest and status_effect_replay_selftest passed. See docs/protocol-audit/VALIDATION.md and test-results-v3.txt. This is Perlin runtime validation, not differential execution of the native client.

limits: Native conclusions are for the GUID-matched1.26.51.1 executable, protocol2193; tests on944/2225 exercise Perlin compatibility paths and do not establish matching binaries for those versions.

Perlin only rewinds across retained stamp and stamp+1 records. Native missing-frame/current-frame fallback and broader ECS reconciliation have additional behavior; failed-send gaps are not claimed to be a complete native history implementation.

The latest-stamp implementation reconstructs the live evaluated component from Perlin’s last retained simulation record. This fixes the common no-next-record acknowledgment case without substituting raw server/current-model values; no dynamic reference-client trace was run.
The new consumer does not add player jump-strength, friction or bounciness attribute physics. Their native map entries are recorded as evidence for separately verified work.
The existing movement modifier evaluator is extracted and reused; this change does not claim that every modifier operation, effect amplifier, collision or world state is now identical.
No successful anticheat/server trial or cause of a prior ban is established by these tests.
